In detail

This is the one Sant Martí barri repeatedly flagged in real press/analysis as a higher-crime area. An idealista.com analysis (Feb 2026), citing Mossos data and 2025 security studies, lists it among Barcelona's most-flagged neighbourhoods for higher-than-average thefts, robberies, vandalism and fights, and references a shooting investigated nearby in August 2025. Earlier coverage documents a masked gang using crowbars to force entry into homes over roughly two years, a dismantled stolen-phone resale ring, and residents publicly protesting insecurity since at least 2021, including concern about spillover from shootings in the adjacent La Mina estate. Sources checked: idealista.com, 9 Feb 2026; Metrópoli Abierta, 25 Jan 2023 / 1 Oct 2021.

This rating comes from a structured local-source assessment. This specific area was reviewed against credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — and the signals were consolidated across sources rather than taken from any single report, with the reasoning and the sources shown above. Barcelona publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does publish one, Wandroz uses it instead of an assessment. Where a review finds nothing documented, that is recorded as no findings rather than as a safety rating.

Is el Besòs i el Maresme safe?

Wandroz currently rates el Besòs i el Maresme in Barcelona as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Barcelona during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Barcelona at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report.
